heuristics.statement: For the bumped iteration G of proof.md Section 3 (Pollard rho on order-6 automorphism equivalence classes with a partition bump), the classes visited by a trail behave like the iterates of a uniform random mapping on the N'' = 1 + (r-1)/6 classes for (i) collision (birthday) statistics and (ii) per-step uniformity used in the cycle-density and bump-incidence bounds. No short-cycle statistics are assumed: the bump destroys every one-entry-determined cycle (proof.md Section 6.2), and the residual cycle content is bounded by the counting of Section 6.3 and measured exactly at toy scale by functional-graph census.
heuristics.support: The v2 form of this heuristic failed because the plain walk's two-cycle content is systematic, not random-mapping-like; v3 narrows the heuristic's scope to the two uses above and proves the cycle structure separately. Empirically: the included experiment's bumped-walk attack run matches the birthday model in the total-steps metric (success 0.627 against the 0.405 budget target, mean visited 255.9 against the predicted 262.2), and its census mode finds the plain walk's two-cycle states tracking N''/(6J) (484/232/106/66 at J=16/32/64/128 against 456/228/114/57) while the bumped walk's are 0/0/2/0 (proof.md Section 8).

limitations: Analytic construction; no full-size execution or independent qualification.

Success probability 0.405 is conditional on the disclosed random-mapping heuristic H1 as scoped in claim.json and proof.md; the cycle-avoidance, collision algebra, exceptional-step enforcement and scalar schedule are exact.
The declared exponential memory (2^113 bytes) is required; this is not a practical break of secp256k1.
Per-step instruction bounds are analytical upper bounds in the cost model's scalar AArch64 instruction basis, not measurements of an implementation.
